_comment: Mutation sweep for V-BRK-022 -- every verb in the envelope's closed enum executes end to end, and the verb set is discovered from the enum rather than restated. Run: python3 dev/mutate.py verification/mutants/V-BRK-022.json. Every row names the test that must fail; see dev/mutate.py for why rc != 0 is not a catch.

mutants.why: THE property. Before this unit, create/apply/patch passed and delete/scale could not complete; a check that took its verb list from a table would have printed green on exactly this. Discovery from the enum is what makes a shrunk enum visible.
The vacuity direction. An empty enum makes the loop body unreachable, and a check that iterates nothing passes.
The delete gap this unit closed. Without ExpectAbsent the kind's own row runs, mustGet reads NotFound as VerdictFailed, and a delete that worked is rolled back by recreating what it deleted.
Same gap, one layer down: the driver's chooser ignoring the flag. Kind cannot answer this -- a Deployment verifies as a rollout when applied and as an absence when deleted.

edits.find:
func predicateFor(t Target) Predicate {
	if t.ExpectAbsent {
edits.replace:
func predicateFor(t Target) Predicate {
	if false {

mutants.why: The absence row's own failure direction. Reporting a delete that did nothing as satisfied is worse than reporting a good delete as failed: nothing rolls back and the journal says it worked.
'I could not look' reported as 'it is gone'. The one error that IS an absence is the replaced-uid sentinel; treating every error that way verifies a delete against a dead API server.
The scale gap this unit closed. A nil baseline makes workloadPredicate Indeterminate, the settle window expires, and EVERY Deployment or StatefulSet action rolls back after appearing to work.
Captured at step 3 and dropped at step 10 is indistinguishable from never captured, and reads as covered because the capture has its own tests.
A create's object had no pods, so zero is the right baseline and nil is a rollback of every Deployment create that worked.
Degrading to nil lands the write and then undoes it at the end of the settle window. Refusing before step 5 costs a retry.

edits.find:

mutants.why: Two tables of kinds that nothing compares are two tables that will disagree. A StatefulSet with a workload predicate and no baseline row verifies as Indeterminate forever.
[[LSN-040]] itself, in its second form: classify's copy of the verb set drifting from the envelope's with nothing comparing them. A rule naming the extra verb reads as a control and matches nothing.

mutants.why: An exception with a placeholder justification is the LSN-041 shape -- the sentence claiming a control is the reason nobody writes the control. A declaration with nothing in it must not satisfy the declaration requirement.

mutants.why: What makes the `cloud` divergence a property rather than a claim. The verb matching nothing is safe only while no cloudTarget reaches the classifier.

mutants.why: The other polarity of M3, and the more dangerous one: every non-delete verified by whether its object has GONE. A create whose object is present reads as failed and rolls back, and only a check that drives all five verbs sees both directions.
